Subject: Onboarding: model shortlist & traffic context (follow-up)

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from the FinBridge product team:

- Shortlist: we'd like your recommended model candidates (size/quantization variants) that preserve our PII redaction and multi-turn summary quality.
- Context needs: our primary flow is a 4–6 message support thread (avg 320 tokens convo, with ~1–2KB of structured metadata per request). We expect many short bursts and occasional long threads when resolving disputes.
- Token volume: current MVP traffic is roughly 45k queries/day (peak 2x), average user session ~3 prompts. We need a 6-week forecast to align procurement and Dedicated pool sizing — can you put together a conservative token baseline + peak scenario?

Also attached the discovery notes and the sample hourly traffic snapshot. Happy to run a small sample dataset if that helps.

Next steps: can you propose a shortlist + an initial 6-week token benchmark plan we can review with procurement? Ideally we want clear SLO/latency implications per model choice.

Best,
Alex
Product Lead, FinBridge

Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist & traffic context (follow-up)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the context and the attachments — very helpful. High level plan below; ben and Jordan, tagging you for throughput numbers and rollout sequencing.

1) Model shortlist (recommended order)
   - small/latency-first: Llama2-13B-8k q4_0 (quantized) — good baseline for chat quality at low cost, 8k context sufficient for most sessions.
   - medium/balanced: Mistral-7B-16k fp16 — better summarization coherence for multi-turn dispute threads.
   - high-quality/fallback: OpenRedwood-30B-32k (fp16 or 4-bit for Dedicated) — use for long dispute threads or when precision matters.

Rationale: FinBridge's typical sessions are short but occasionally require multi-turn resolution and precise entity handling. We recommend starting with the 13B quantized baseline for most traffic and keep the 30B model as a slow-path fallback (automated routing by intent/confidence).

2) Context length guidance
   - Default request window: last 3 turns + metadata (approx 350–500 tokens).
   - For dispute resolution: up to 8 turns (~1,800 tokens) with a server-side truncation policy and prefix caching for common system prompts.

3) 6-week token benchmark plan (proposal)
   - Week 0 (pilot): 10k queries/day, run split test between 13B q4_0 and Mistral-7B-16k to validate quality delta.
   - Weeks 1–3 (ramp): expand to 35k queries/day, observe latency P95 and token distribution.
   - Weeks 4–6 (forecast-run): ramp to target 45k queries/day (peak 90k), run 72-hour high-load simulation for peak provisioning.

Deliverables from Redwood:
   - Token baseline CSV (per-route, per-model) with simulated latency bands.
   - Small-run evaluation pack with redaction recall precision for each model.
   - Recommendation for Dedicated pool size with safety margin (ben to add specifics).

Can you confirm FinBridge is OK with the pilot split and the proposed measurement windows? If so we’ll schedule the first benchmark run and share the CSV outputs.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

--

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist & token benchmark plan (numbers)

Looping in numbers we discussed. Quick notes:

- Baseline token per request (median): 420 tokens (includes prompt + 3-turn context + metadata).
- Dispute thread median: 1,650 tokens.
- Average completion tokens per response: 60 tokens (we'll cap to 256 for safety in pilot).

Sizing (conservative) for 45k q/day:
- Request tokens/day (median estimate): 45,000 * 420 = ~18.9M request tokens/day.
- Completion tokens/day (assuming 1.2 responses per query avg * 60 tokens): 45,000 * 72 = ~3.24M completion tokens/day.
- Total tokens/day: ~22.1M -> weekly ~154.7M -> 6-week ~928.2M tokens.

Peak scenario (2x peak factor):
- Peak day tokens: ~44.2M tokens. Design Dedicated with headroom for 1.5x to 2x depending on SLA.

Model cost/latency considerations (rough):
- Llama2-13B-q4_0 (13B q4): P95 token latency low; expected avg TTFB for small requests ~80–120ms on our optimized runtime. Good cost per token.
- Mistral-7B-16k fp16: slightly higher per-token cost for long contexts but better multi-turn coherence.
- OpenRedwood-30B: reserve for slow-path only (higher cost, use for <5% of traffic initially).

Attachments: I exported a quick CSV with per-route token breakdown and hourly ramp plan (attached: token-benchmark-6wk.csv). I recommend we trigger the pilot this Friday, run the 72-hour high-load simulation in week 4, and freeze model routing rules before week 5.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: token-benchmark-6wk.csv
